name: Scotch Game
description: A beginner-friendly open game that teaches central pawn breaks, active development, and simple tactical play after 1.e4 e5.

branches.title: Main Line: Break With d4
branches.description: Learn the default Scotch idea: develop, then challenge the center with d4.

moves.title: Claim the center
moves.explanation: Controls d5 and f5 while opening lines for the bishop and queen. e4 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. The Scotch opens the center early, so piece activity and safe king placement matter more than pawn counting.

moves.title: Black mirrors
moves.explanation: Black also takes central space, creating an open-game structure. e5 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. The Scotch opens the center early, so piece activity and safe king placement matter more than pawn counting.

moves.title: Develop with pressure
moves.explanation: Develops a knight and attacks e5 before making the central break. Nf3 develops a knight to f3. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Black defends e5
moves.explanation: Black develops and protects the e5 pawn. Nc6 develops a knight to c6. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Break open the center
moves.explanation: d4 challenges e5 and opens lines. The Scotch teaches active central play after development. d4 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. The Scotch opens the center early, so piece activity and safe king placement matter more than pawn counting.

moves.title: Trade or capture on d4
moves.explanation: exd4 shows how trades enter the opening. This is an equal trade. Equal trades are good when they improve your structure, open a file, or remove an active enemy piece. After a trade, ask which file opened and which piece should improve next.

moves.title: Trade or capture on d4
moves.explanation: Nxd4 shows how trades enter the opening. This capture should only be played because it gains time, opens lines, or solves a concrete problem. After a trade, ask which file opened and which piece should improve next.

moves.title: Develop to c3
moves.explanation: Nc3 develops a knight to c3. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Develop to b4
moves.explanation: Bb4 develops a bishop to b4. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Connect the pieces
moves.explanation: Qd2 is a supportive queen move after development has started. The queen helps connect rooks and protect key squares instead of wandering out early.

moves.title: Get the king safe
moves.explanation: O-O gets the king safe and brings a rook closer to the center. This is the bridge from opening to middlegame: now look for your worst piece, your safest trade, and your best pawn break.

hints: Follow the highlighted move and say the idea out loud.
After each move, check king safety, center control, and piece activity.
When a trade appears, ask what file opens and which piece improves next.
